column1: # p217 - ACTION QN: the 67 remaining ungranted rows, probed through the ONE channel left unread -
#        the repository's own README, read as TEXT.
#         README.md, readme.md, README.MD, README.rst, README.txt, README  -> first 200 wins.
#         Then grep the body for a licence-shaped statement and classify FROM THE SECTION BODY,
#         not from the heading (a bare "## License" heading carries no grant and must be opened).
# NOTE (carried from ACTION QN's own registration, and it governs every row below):
#        A PROSE CLAIM IS NOT A GRANT. Nothing here is promoted to a usable licence. Each hit is
#        recorded as a CLASS. `mcp-powerschool` is the archived precedent for the distinction.
# population 67 | README reachable 64 | non-public 3 | licence-shaped prose hits 19
#   PROSE-CLAIM-DANGLING  - README names a grant AND points at a LICENSE file that is NOT in the tree
#   PROSE-CLAIM-BARE      - README names a grant, no pointer, no file in tree
#   PROSE-CLAIM-QUALIFIED - README names a grant AND attaches a term the named licence does not contain
#   PROSE-CLAIM-SCOPED    - README names a grant for PART of the repo only (curation vs linked content)
#   PROSE-CLAIM-CONFLICT  - two channels INSIDE the one README name different licences
#   PROSE-THIRD-PARTY     - the licence section covers dependencies only; no own-project grant
#   GRANT-REFUSED         - README affirmatively REFUSES a grant. This is not an absence.
#   DOMAIN-NOUN           - false positive: "licence" is the repo's subject matter, not its grant
#   NO-PROSE              - README reachable, no licence-shaped statement
#   NON-PUBLIC            - no README served and the address does not resolve / demands credentials
